records.source: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: The word which came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh, saying:
pieces: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

L.1: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying:

R.1: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah:

decisions.choice: the word that came to Jeremiah: the heading of a new collection, the promises of restoration in chapters 30-33
decisions.reason: This heading opens messages in 7:1, 11:1 and 21:1. Here it begins a group of chapters (30-33) that are almost all promise: the LORD will bring his people home, heal them and make a new covenant with them. The chapters before it are mostly warnings of judgment.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying: / This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD: / This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah:
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this heading (as in 7:1 and 11:1). Balanced makes the heading a sentence and drops "saying", which only introduces what follows, and Readable says it plainly.

records.heading: The exiles will come home

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּתָב־לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל־סֵֽפֶר׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, saying: Write for yourself all the words which I have spoken to you into a book.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: "Write down in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

L.2: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: "Write for yourself all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.

R.2: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: "Write down on a scroll all the words I have spoken to you.

decisions.choice: book: a written document, in Jeremiah's time a scroll
decisions.reason: The word means any written record: a letter (29:1), a deed (32:10) or a longer work. Books were written on rolls of leather or papyrus, like the scroll Jeremiah dictated to Baruch (36:2).

decisions.choice: all the words I have spoken to you: the messages of hope that follow
decisions.reason: Verse 4 says "these are the words", pointing ahead to the poems of chapters 30-31. Writing them down keeps the promise for the people who will see the "days" of verse 3, after the exile.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the LORD's words in this prose introduction
decisions.reason: Verses 1-4 are prose, so the LORD's command and promise (verses 2-3) are quoted as prose quotes speech. The poems that begin at verse 5 follow the book's rule for oracles and take no outer quotation marks.

decisions.choice: on a scroll
decisions.reason: Readable names the kind of book Jeremiah would have written on (m1).

records.source: כִּ֠י הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְ֠שַׁבְתִּי אֶת־שְׁב֨וּת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֗ים אֶל־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם וִֽירֵשֽׁוּהָ׃פ
records.gloss: For look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and I will turn back [the] captivity of my people Israel and Judah, says Yahweh, and I will bring them back to the land which I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.
pieces: For the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will restore the fortunes of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel and Judah, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will possess it."

L.3: For look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will restore the fortunes of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel and Judah, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will take possession of it."

R.3: The time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will make things good again for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, Israel and Judah. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and it will be theirs again."

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes: turn the people's ruin into well-being, including bringing the exiles home
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats one root, "turn the turning". It means a complete reversal from ruin to blessing; it is used of Job, who was never a captive (Job 42:10), and of the land and people as a whole (Deuteronomy 30:3; Psalm 126:4). Because the noun sounds like the word for captivity, it was long read "bring back the captivity", and here the return from exile is part of what is meant, as the rest of the verse says. Jeremiah uses the phrase in 29:14 and through the promises of chapters 30-33 (30:18; 31:23; 32:44; 33:7, 11, 26).

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah: the whole people, both the northern kingdom and the southern
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom, Israel, had been taken into exile by Assyria a century earlier (2 Kings 17:6), and Judah was going into exile in Babylon. The promise covers both, as do 3:18 and 31:27, 31.

decisions.choice: the land I gave their fathers, and they will possess it: the gift of the land made new
decisions.reason: The words recall the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the call to "possess" the land in Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy 1:8; 30:5). Exile seemed to undo that gift; here it is given again.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again for (R)
decisions.reason: One wording for this phrase wherever it returns in Jeremiah, as in Deuteronomy 30:3. Readable says what the phrase means (m1).

decisions.choice: the second "says the LORD" left out
decisions.reason: The verse names the LORD as speaker twice. Readable gives the formula once, at the start, to keep the sentence short; the meaning is unchanged.

records.source: וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶל־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And these [are] the words which Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.
pieces: These are the words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke concerning Israel and Judah:

L.4: And these [are] the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah:

R.4: These are the messages {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave about Israel and Judah:

decisions.choice: these are the words: a second heading, introducing the poems that follow
decisions.reason: After the command to write (verses 2-3), this line introduces the poems of 30:5-31:40, which speak to both parts of the people, as verse 3 did.

records.source: כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חֲרָדָ֖ה שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ פַּ֖חַד וְאֵ֥ין שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: [A] sound of trembling we have heard, dread, and there is not peace.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q "We have heard a cry of panic, \q of terror, and there is no peace."

L.5: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q "A sound of trembling we have heard, \q terror, and there is no peace."

R.5: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q "We hear people screaming in fear. \q Everyone is terrified, and there is no peace."

decisions.choice: we have heard: the voice of the frightened people, quoted by the LORD
decisions.reason: The poem opens in the middle of panic. The LORD quotes those who hear the sounds of war: the people, or the prophet speaking with them (compare 4:19-21; 8:15). The promise comes only after the terror has been heard (verse 7).

decisions.choice: a sound of trembling, dread: the noise and the feeling of panic
decisions.reason: The first word can mean a voice or a sound, here the cries and noise of people shaking with fear. The second is sudden dread (49:5; Isaiah 24:17).

decisions.choice: there is no peace: no safety or well-being
decisions.reason: The words answer the false prophets, who said "Peace, peace" when there was no peace (6:14; 8:11, 15). Peace here is the whole well-being of the people.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks around the people's cry
decisions.reason: Under the book's speech rule the LORD's own words in the oracle take no quotation marks, but speech he quotes inside it does (m1).

decisions.choice: people screaming ... Everyone is terrified
decisions.reason: Readable names who is making the sound and who is afraid, which the Hebrew leaves to the picture.

records.source: שַׁאֲלוּ־נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ אִם־יֹלֵ֖ד זָכָ֑ר מַדּוּעַ֩ רָאִ֨יתִי כָל־גֶּ֜בֶר יָדָ֤יו עַל־חֲלָצָיו֙ כַּיּ֣וֹלֵדָ֔ה וְנֶהֶפְכ֥וּ כָל־פָּנִ֖ים לְיֵרָקֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Ask please and see whether giving birth [is a] male; why have I seen every man, his hands on his loins, like [one] giving birth, and turned all faces to paleness?
pieces: Ask and see: \q can a man give birth? \q Then why do I see every man with his hands pressed to his sides like a woman in labor, \q every face gone deathly pale?

L.6: Ask now and see \q whether a male gives birth. \q Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman giving birth, \q and every face turned pale?

R.6: Ask around and find out: \q Can a man have a baby? \q Then why do I see every man holding his sides in pain like a woman giving birth? \q Why has every face turned pale?

decisions.choice: can a male give birth? like a woman in labor: men gripped by pain and terror they cannot escape
decisions.reason: Labor pains are the prophets' picture for sudden, overwhelming terror (4:31; 6:24; 13:21; 22:23; Isaiah 13:8). The question is meant to sound absurd: men cannot give birth, yet every man is clutching himself like a woman in labor.

decisions.choice: man: a grown man, one expected to be strong
decisions.reason: This word for man often stresses strength (Psalm 34:9; Jeremiah 17:5). That the strong are bent double makes the picture sharper.

decisions.choice: paleness: the gray or sickly color of a face drained of blood
decisions.reason: The word is used of crops struck by blight (Deuteronomy 28:22; Amos 4:9). Here it is the color of faces white with fear (compare Joel 2:6).

decisions.choice: hands pressed to his sides (B); holding his sides in pain (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "loins", the waist and lower back, where a woman in labor holds herself. Balanced and Readable say "sides" for a modern reader, and Readable adds "in pain", which the comparison implies.

records.source: ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מֵאַ֣יִן כָּמֹ֑הוּ וְעֵֽת־צָרָ֥ה הִיא֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִמֶּ֖נָּה יִוָּשֵֽׁעַ׃
records.gloss: Woe! For great [is] the day the that, from there is not like it; and [a] time of distress it [is] for Jacob, and from it he will be saved.
pieces: Woe! That day is great; there is no other like it. \q It is a time of distress for Jacob, \q yet he will be saved out of it.

L.7: Woe! For great [is] that day, with none like it; \q it [is] a time of distress for Jacob, \q yet out of it he will be saved.

R.7: How terrible that day will be! There will be no other day like it. \q It will be a time of great trouble for the people of Jacob, \q but they will be saved from it.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of alarm and grief, here addressed to no one
decisions.reason: The same cry begins laments for the dead (22:18) and warnings of judgment (Isaiah 5:8). Here it names no one; it is a cry at the sight of the coming day.

decisions.choice: that day is great, with none like it: the day of the LORD's judgment
decisions.reason: "That day" is the day of the LORD, when he acts in judgment (Joel 2:2, 11; Amos 5:18-20; Zephaniah 1:14-15). Daniel 12:1 speaks in similar words of "a time of distress such as has never been".

decisions.choice: a time of distress for Jacob, yet out of it he will be saved: judgment and rescue in the same day
decisions.reason: The day falls on Jacob too, but it does not end him: he will be saved out of it. The verse turns the poem from terror to promise, which verses 8-11 then spell out.

decisions.choice: Jacob: the whole people descended from Jacob
decisions.reason: As often in the prophets, the ancestor's name stands for the nation (verse 10; Isaiah 41:8).

decisions.choice: How terrible that day will be! ... the people of Jacob ... they
decisions.reason: Readable gives the cry its meaning, as the book does for this word, and says "the people of Jacob", as Isaiah's Readable does, so the plural "they" follows (m4).

records.source: וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם׀יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק וְלֹא־יַעַבְדוּ־ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it will be on the day the that, declares Yahweh of hosts, I will break his yoke from on your neck, and your bonds I will tear off, and not will make serve him again strangers.
pieces: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q I will break his yoke from your neck and tear off your bonds, \q and foreigners will no longer make him serve them.

L.8: And it will be on that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q [that] I will break his yoke from off your neck, and your bonds I will tear off, \q and strangers will no longer make him serve [them].

R.8: On that day, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q I will break the yoke that is on your neck and tear off your chains. \q Foreigners will never again force {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to serve them.

decisions.choice: his yoke ... your neck ... him: the oppressor's yoke on Jacob, who is first spoken to and then spoken of
decisions.reason: "His yoke" is the yoke of the foreign master, the king of Babylon (27:8, 11; 28:14). "Your neck" and "your bonds" speak to Jacob, and "him" at the end speaks of Jacob; such changes of person are common in Hebrew poetry.

decisions.choice: I will break the yoke and tear off the bonds: the reversal of chapters 27-28
decisions.reason: Jeremiah wore a yoke as a sign of Babylon's rule, and when Hananiah broke it, the LORD said he would put an iron yoke on the nations (27:2; 28:10-14). Now the LORD himself promises to break it, in words that recall the exodus (Leviticus 26:13) and 2:20.

decisions.choice: make him serve: force Jacob into servitude
decisions.reason: With this preposition the verb means to make someone work for you, to hold them in bondage (25:14; 27:7). Verse 9 answers with the same verb: they will serve the LORD instead.

decisions.choice: serve, as in verse 9
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the verb "serve" so that the contrast with verse 9 can be heard: no longer serving foreigners, but serving the LORD (m3).

decisions.choice: the yoke that is on your neck ... my people
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the unexplained "his" and says "my people" for "him", so the reader can follow who is meant (m1).

records.source: וְעָ֣בְד֔וּ אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֵת֙ דָּוִ֣ד מַלְכָּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָקִ֖ים לָהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And they will serve Yahweh their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
pieces: They will serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God instead \q and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

L.9: And they will serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God \q and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

R.9: Instead they will serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God \q and their king from David's family, whom I will raise up for them.

decisions.choice: David their king: the promised king of David's line
decisions.reason: David had died some four hundred years before. The promise is of a ruler from his family who will be a second David (23:5-6; 33:15-17; Ezekiel 34:23-24; 37:24-25; Hosea 3:5). The New Testament sees this promise fulfilled in Jesus, the son of David (Luke 1:32-33; Acts 13:22-23).

decisions.choice: raise up: bring to power, appoint
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God setting up a leader or king (23:4-5; Judges 2:16; Amos 2:11). It does not mean raising from the dead.

decisions.choice: they will serve the LORD: the opposite of serving foreigners
decisions.reason: The verse picks up the verb of verse 8. Freed from foreign masters, the people will give their service to their own God and to the king he gives them.

decisions.choice: their king from David's family
decisions.reason: Readable says what "David" means here (m1), so the reader does not think of David himself coming back.

decisions.choice: Instead
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the contrast with verse 8 that the simple "and" carries (m3).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל־תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם־יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל־תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, declares Yahweh, and do not be dismayed, Israel; for look, I [am] saving you from afar, and your offspring from [the] land of their captivity; and Jacob will return and be quiet and be at ease, and there [will be] none making [him] afraid.
pieces: So you, Jacob {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, do not be afraid, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; do not be dismayed, Israel. \q For I will save you from a far country, and your descendants from the land where they are captives. \q Jacob will come home and have quiet and rest, and no one will make him afraid.

L.10: And you, do not fear, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do not be dismayed, Israel, \q for look, I am saving you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. \q And Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, and there will be no one to make [him] afraid.

R.10: So do not be afraid, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Israel, do not be frightened. \q I will save you from a land far away. I will save your children from the land where they are prisoners. \q The people of Jacob will come home. They will live in peace and safety, and no one will frighten them.

decisions.choice: do not fear, my servant Jacob: words repeated at 46:27-28
decisions.reason: Verses 10-11 return almost word for word at the end of the oracle against Egypt (46:27-28). They also echo Isaiah's words to Israel as the LORD's servant (Isaiah 41:8-10; 43:5; 44:2).

decisions.choice: my servant: Israel as the people the LORD has chosen and keeps
decisions.reason: To be the LORD's servant is to belong to him and be under his protection. It is a title of honor here, not of bondage (Isaiah 41:8-9; 44:1-2).

decisions.choice: verses 10-11 kept here, as the Hebrew text has them
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah does not have verses 10-11 in this chapter; it has them only in its form of 46:27-28. The Hebrew text, which this translation follows, has them in both places.

decisions.choice: I am saving you from far away: a sure promise, spoken as if it were already under way
decisions.reason: The participle describes what the LORD is about to do and is already setting in motion. "From far away" means from a distant land, the land of exile.

decisions.choice: do not fear / do not be afraid; do not be dismayed / do not be frightened
decisions.reason: These verses are to keep one wording here and at 46:27-28 (m1), so that a reader hears the same promise in both places.

decisions.choice: The people of Jacob ... They ... them
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Jacob", as Isaiah's Readable does, so that the plural pronouns follow.

records.source: כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֣ם׀אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא־אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ׃פ
records.gloss: For with you I [am], declares Yahweh, to save you; for I will make [a] full end of all the nations where I have scattered you there, but you I will not make [a] full end [of]; and I will discipline you in justice, and leaving unpunished I will not leave you unpunished.
pieces: For I am with you to save you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will bring to an end all the nations among whom I scattered you, but you I will not bring to an end. \q I will discipline you, but justly, \q and I will not let you go unpunished.

L.11: For I [am] with you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to save you. \q For I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but of you I will not make a full end. \q I will discipline you in just measure, \q and I will by no means leave you unpunished.

R.11: I am with you, and I will save you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will completely destroy all the nations where I scattered you. But I will not completely destroy you. \q I will correct you, but I will be fair, \q and I will not let you escape all punishment.

decisions.choice: I am with you to save you: the promise first given to Jeremiah, now given to the people
decisions.reason: At his call the LORD told Jeremiah, "I am with you to rescue you" (1:8, 19; 15:20). Here the same assurance is given to the whole people.

decisions.choice: a full end: complete destruction
decisions.reason: The word means a finishing off, total ruin (4:27; 5:10, 18). The nations that held Israel will come to such an end; Israel will not.

decisions.choice: discipline you in justice: correct you in fair measure, not to destroy you
decisions.reason: Jeremiah prayed, "Correct me, LORD, but in justice, not in your anger, or you will bring me to nothing" (10:24). The LORD's discipline has a limit and a purpose.

decisions.choice: leaving unpunished I will not leave you unpunished: I will certainly not let you go free of punishment
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to make it emphatic. The words recall the LORD's self-description in Exodus 34:7 and Numbers 14:18: he forgives, but he does not simply ignore guilt.

decisions.choice: I will correct you, but I will be fair
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "in justice" means here (m3).

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: Incurable [is] your fracture, grievous [is] your wound.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Your injury cannot be cured; \q your wound is severe.

L.12: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Incurable [is] your fracture, \q grievous your wound.

R.12: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Your injury cannot be healed. \q Your wound is very bad.

decisions.choice: your (spoken to a woman): Zion, the city and its people, pictured as a wounded woman
decisions.reason: From here to verse 17 the one spoken to is feminine, and verse 17 names her: Zion. The people called Jacob in verses 7-11 are now pictured as a woman broken by her wounds.

decisions.choice: incurable fracture: a break that no one can mend, the ruin of the nation
decisions.reason: The noun means a break or a shattering, used for the ruin of the people (8:21; 10:19; 14:17). "Incurable" is the word Jeremiah used of his own pain (15:18). By any human means the wound cannot be healed; verse 17 says who will heal it.

decisions.choice: injury ... severe (B); injury ... very bad (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of a broken bone, "fracture". Balanced and Readable say "injury", which covers the same hurt in plainer words, here and in verse 15.

records.heading: Healing for an incurable wound

records.source: אֵֽין־דָּ֥ן דִּינֵ֖ךְ לְמָז֑וֹר רְפֻא֥וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: There is not [one] pleading your cause for [a] sore; remedies, new flesh, there is not for you.
pieces: There is no one to take up your cause, no one for your sore; \q there are no remedies, no healing for you.

L.13: There is no one pleading your cause for [your] sore; \q remedies, new skin, there are none for you.

R.13: No one speaks up for you or cares for your sores. \q No medicine can help you. Nothing can heal you.

decisions.choice: plead your cause: take up your case, as an advocate does in court
decisions.reason: The verb and noun come from the same root and are used of defending someone's rights (5:28; 22:16). The poem mixes the courtroom with the sickbed: Zion has no one to speak for her and no one to treat her.

decisions.choice: "for a sore" belongs with the first line, as the Hebrew accents divide the verse
alternatives: for your sore there are remedies, but no new skin for you
decisions.reason: The accents place the main pause after "for a sore". Another way of dividing the verse links it to what follows: "for your sore there are remedies, but no new skin for you." Either way, Zion's wound will not heal.

decisions.choice: new skin: the fresh skin that grows over a wound as it heals
decisions.reason: The word is used again in 46:11, "there is no healing for you". It is the sign that a wound is closing; here there is none.

decisions.choice: speaks up for you or cares for your sores
decisions.reason: Readable puts both pictures, the advocate and the one who treats the wound, into plain words (m1).

records.source: כָּל־מְאַהֲבַ֣יִךְ שְׁכֵח֔וּךְ אוֹתָ֖ךְ לֹ֣א יִדְרֹ֑שׁוּ כִּי֩ מַכַּ֨ת אוֹיֵ֤ב הִכִּיתִיךְ֙ מוּסַ֣ר אַכְזָרִ֔י עַ֚ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ עָצְמ֖וּ חַטֹּאתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: All your lovers have forgotten you; you they do not seek; for [with the] blow of an enemy I have struck you, [the] discipline of a cruel [one], because of [the] greatness of your iniquity, numerous [are] your sins.
pieces: All your lovers have forgotten you; \q they do not care about you. \q For I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with the punishment of a cruel foe, \q because your guilt is great \q and your sins are many.

L.14: All your lovers have forgotten you; \q they do not seek you. \q For with the blow of an enemy I have struck you, with the discipline of a cruel one, \q because your iniquity is great, \q [because] your sins are numerous.

R.14: All the nations you loved have forgotten you. \q They do not care about you. \q I have hit you as an enemy would. I have punished you harshly, like someone cruel, \q because your sins are so many and so great.

decisions.choice: your lovers: the nations Judah trusted as allies instead of the LORD
decisions.reason: Jeremiah pictures Judah's alliances as a woman's lovers (4:30; 22:20, 22). The help she looked for from Egypt and others failed her (2:36-37).

decisions.choice: I have struck you with the blow of an enemy: the LORD himself stands behind the enemy's attack
decisions.reason: The defeat by Babylon was not out of the LORD's control: he says he dealt the blow, as an enemy would. Lamentations 2:4-5 uses the same bold picture of the LORD acting like an enemy.

decisions.choice: the discipline of a cruel one: punishment as harsh as a cruel master gives
decisions.reason: The noun is the usual word for discipline or correction (2:30; 5:3). Here it is heavy and painful, though verse 11 has already said it has a limit.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The wording for this word set for Isaiah and Jeremiah. Readable joins "iniquity" and "sins" into one phrase.

decisions.choice: All the nations you loved
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "lovers" are (m1).

records.source: מַה־תִּזְעַק֙ עַל־שִׁבְרֵ֔ךְ אָנ֖וּשׁ מַכְאֹבֵ֑ךְ עַ֣ל׀רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֵ֗ךְ עָֽצְמוּ֙ חַטֹּאתַ֔יִךְ עָשִׂ֥יתִי אֵ֖לֶּה לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Why do you cry out over your fracture? Incurable [is] your pain; because of [the] greatness of your iniquity, numerous [are] your sins, I have done these [things] to you.
pieces: Why cry out over your injury? \q Your pain cannot be cured. \q Because your guilt is great and your sins are many, \q I have done these things to you.

L.15: Why do you cry out over your fracture? \q Your pain [is] incurable. \q Because of the greatness of your iniquity, [because] your sins are numerous, \q I have done these things to you.

R.15: Why do you cry out because you are hurt? \q Your pain cannot be healed. \q I have done this to you, \q because your sins are so many and so great.

decisions.choice: why do you cry out: a question that points to the cause of the wound
decisions.reason: The question does not forbid grief. It asks Zion to see why she is suffering: the wound came because of her sin, and the LORD sent it. The second half of the verse repeats the end of verse 14 and adds "I have done these things to you".

decisions.choice: verse 15 kept, as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah does not have this verse, which largely repeats verses 12 and 14. The Hebrew text, which this translation follows, has it.

decisions.choice: I have done this to you, because your sins are so many and so great.
decisions.reason: Readable puts the main statement before the reason, which is easier to follow, and joins "guilt" and "sins" as in verse 14.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן כָּל־אֹכְלַ֨יִךְ֙ יֵאָכֵ֔לוּ וְכָל־צָרַ֥יִךְ כֻּלָּ֖ם בַּשְּׁבִ֣י יֵלֵ֑כוּ וְהָי֤וּ שֹׁאסַ֨יִךְ֙ לִמְשִׁסָּ֔ה וְכָל־בֹּזְזַ֖יִךְ אֶתֵּ֥ן לָבַֽז׃
records.gloss: Therefore all [those] devouring you will be devoured, and all your foes, all of them, into captivity will go; and [those] plundering you will become plunder, and all [those] despoiling you I will give as spoil.
pieces: Yet all who devour you will be devoured, \q and all your foes, every one of them, will go into captivity. \q Those who plunder you will become plunder, \q and all who prey on you I will hand over as prey.

L.16: Therefore all who devour you will be devoured, \q and all your foes, every one of them, will go into captivity; \q and those who plunder you will become plunder, \q and all who prey on you I will give as prey.

R.16: But everyone who destroys you will be destroyed. \q All your enemies will be taken away as prisoners. \q People who rob you will be robbed. \q I will let others rob everyone who steals from you.

decisions.choice: therefore: the turn from judgment to rescue, which comes from the LORD's purpose and not from Zion's merit
decisions.reason: After verse 15 one expects more punishment, but the word introduces the reversal. Some take it as a strong "yet" or "surely". Either way, the reason for the change is the LORD's own decision to heal (verse 17), not a change in Zion.

decisions.choice: devour: destroy, as a wild animal tears its prey
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses the word for the nations that "devoured Jacob" (10:25; 50:7, 17). What they did will be done to them (2:3).

decisions.choice: captivity, plunder, prey: the oppressors suffer what they inflicted
decisions.reason: Each line turns a crime back on those who did it. The same measure-for-measure justice is promised for Babylon (25:12-14; 50:15, 29).

decisions.choice: Yet (B); But (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the turn in the poem with a word of contrast (m1); Literal keeps "therefore".

records.source: כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִדָּחָה֙ קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֔ךְ צִיּ֣וֹן הִ֔יא דֹּרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: For I will bring up new flesh for you, and from your wounds I will heal you, declares Yahweh; for 'Banished one' they have called you: 'Zion [is] it; [one] seeking for her there is not.'
pieces: But I will restore you to health and heal your wounds, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because they have called you an outcast: \q "This is Zion; no one cares about her."

L.17: For I will bring up healing for you, and from your wounds I will heal you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because they have called you "Outcast": \q "It is Zion; there is no one who seeks her."

R.17: But I will make you well again. I will heal your wounds, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People have called you "the one thrown away." \q They say, "This is Zion. No one cares about her."

decisions.choice: bring up healing: make new flesh grow over the wound
decisions.reason: The noun is the fresh flesh that forms as a wound heals; it "comes up" over the injury (8:22; 33:6). The wound no one could heal (verses 12-13) the LORD himself will heal.

decisions.choice: I will heal you: the one who struck is the one who heals
decisions.reason: The LORD sent the blow (verses 14-15), and he alone can mend it (compare Hosea 6:1; Deuteronomy 32:39).

decisions.choice: because they have called you an outcast: the nations' scorn is the reason the LORD acts
decisions.reason: The LORD heals Zion because others have written her off. Their taunt, "no one cares about her", will be proved false (compare 33:24-26).

decisions.choice: outcast: one driven away and abandoned
decisions.reason: The word is used of scattered sheep driven from the flock (23:2-3; 49:36). Zion is called the one nobody wants.

decisions.choice: seeks her (L); cares about her (B, R), as "seek" in verse 14
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as in verse 14, where Zion's lovers do not "seek" her. Each level uses the same word in both verses so the link can be heard. The taunt takes double quotation marks as speech quoted in the oracle.

records.source: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִי־שָׁב֙ שְׁבוּת֙ אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו אֲרַחֵ֑ם וְנִבְנְתָ֥ה עִיר֙ עַל־תִּלָּ֔הּ וְאַרְמ֖וֹן עַל־מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ יֵשֵֽׁב׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Look, I [am] turning back [the] captivity of [the] tents of Jacob, and his dwellings I will have compassion on; and will be rebuilt [the] city on its mound, and [the] palace on its rightful [place] will sit.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I will restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob \q and show compassion to his homes. \q The city will be rebuilt on its ruin mound, \q and the palace will stand where it should.

L.18: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am restoring the fortunes of the tents of Jacob, \q and on his dwellings I will have compassion; \q the city will be rebuilt on its mound, \q and the palace will stand on its rightful site.

R.18: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will make things good again for the families of Jacob. \q I will show kindness to their homes. \q The city will be built again on the hill where its ruins lie. \q The palace will stand in its proper place again.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes: as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The same phrase as verse 3: the LORD will turn ruin into well-being.

decisions.choice: the tents of Jacob, his dwellings: the homes and households of the people
decisions.reason: "Tents" is an old way of speaking of homes, kept from Israel's early life (4:20; 10:20). The promise is for families as well as for the nation.

decisions.choice: its mound: the hill formed by the ruins of earlier cities on the same site
decisions.reason: Cities in Israel were rebuilt again and again on the same spot, so that layer on layer of ruins formed a mound, a tel (Joshua 8:28; 11:13). The ruined city will rise again where it stood, not be moved elsewhere.

decisions.choice: the palace will stand on its rightful site: the chief building restored as it should be
alternatives: the palace will be lived in as it should be
decisions.reason: The noun usually means justice; here it is what is right or proper for the place. The verb "sit" can mean "stand" or "be lived in". Either way the palace or fortress of the city will be in use again where it belongs.

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as verse 3.

decisions.choice: the families of Jacob ... the hill where its ruins lie
decisions.reason: Readable says what "tents" means here (m2) and describes the mound (m3).

records.source: וְיָצָ֥א מֵהֶ֛ם תּוֹדָ֖ה וְק֣וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִ֑ים וְהִרְבִּתִים֙ וְלֹ֣א יִמְעָ֔טוּ וְהִכְבַּדְתִּ֖ים וְלֹ֥א יִצְעָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And will go out from them thanksgiving and [the] sound of [those] making merry; and I will multiply them, and they will not be few; and I will honor them, and they will not be small.
pieces: From them will come songs of thanks and the sound of people celebrating. \q I will make them many, and they will not dwindle; \q I will bring them honor, and they will not be looked down on.

L.19: And from them will go out thanksgiving and the sound of those making merry; \q and I will multiply them, and they will not be few; \q and I will make them honored, and they will not be small.

R.19: You will hear songs of thanks from them and the sound of people celebrating. \q I will make them grow in number. They will not become few. \q I will give them honor. No one will look down on them.

decisions.choice: thanksgiving: songs of thanks, and perhaps the offerings that went with them
decisions.reason: The word is used both for words of praise and for the thank offering brought to the temple (17:26; 33:11).

decisions.choice: the sound of those making merry: the joy that judgment had silenced returns
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had warned that the sounds of joy would cease in Judah (7:34; 16:9; 25:10). Here they come back, as in 31:4 and 33:11.

decisions.choice: I will multiply them: the promise to the ancestors renewed
decisions.reason: The words recall the promise that Abraham's descendants would be many (Genesis 22:17) and the blessing of Leviticus 26:9. The people shrunk by war and exile will grow again.

decisions.choice: they will not be small: they will not be made insignificant or despised
decisions.reason: The verb means to be small or of little account (Zechariah 13:7). Set beside "I will honor them", it means the people will no longer be belittled.

decisions.choice: songs of thanks
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "songs" so that the reader hears the thanks as something voiced aloud, as the parallel "sound" implies (m1).

records.source: וְהָי֤וּ בָנָיו֙ כְּקֶ֔דֶם וַעֲדָת֖וֹ לְפָנַ֣י תִּכּ֑וֹן וּפָ֣קַדְתִּ֔י עַ֖ל כָּל־לֹחֲצָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And his children will be as [in] former [times], and his congregation before me will be established; and I will punish all [those] oppressing him.
pieces: Their children will be as they were long ago; \q their congregation will be firmly established before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and I will punish all who oppress them.

L.20: And his children will be as in former times, \q and his congregation will be established before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and I will punish all who oppress him.

R.20: Their children will be as they were long ago. \q The whole community will stand firm in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence. \q I will punish everyone who is cruel to them.

decisions.choice: his: Jacob, the people
decisions.reason: "His" goes back to Jacob in verse 18. The people as a whole are spoken of as one person.

decisions.choice: his congregation before me: the people gathered as a community in the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Israel gathered in the wilderness (Exodus 12:3; Numbers 1:2). "Before me" means under God's eye and care; the community will be secure.

decisions.choice: punish: call to account
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to someone; with "against" it means to bring them to account for what they did (9:24; 23:2).

decisions.choice: Their ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, since verse 19 already speaks of the people as "them" (m1).

decisions.choice: community
decisions.reason: Readable says "community" for this word, as the terms for these books allow.

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה אַדִּיר֜וֹ מִמֶּ֗נּוּ וּמֹֽשְׁלוֹ֙ מִקִּרְבּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֔א וְהִקְרַבְתִּ֖יו וְנִגַּ֣שׁ אֵלָ֑י כִּי֩ מִ֨י הוּא־זֶ֜ה עָרַ֧ב אֶת־לִבּ֛וֹ לָגֶ֥שֶׁת אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And his noble one will be from him, and his ruler from his midst will go out; and I will bring him near, and he will approach to me; for who [is] he, this [one, who] has pledged his heart to approach to me? declares Yahweh.
pieces: One of their own will be their leader; their ruler will come from among them. \q I will bring him near, and he will come close to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q for who would dare to risk his life by coming close to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And his noble one will be from himself, and his ruler will go out from his midst; \q and I will bring him near, and he will approach {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q For who is he who would pledge his heart to approach {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: Their leader will be one of their own people. Their ruler will come from among them. \q I will invite him to come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and he will come close. \q No one would dare to come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless I invited him, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: from himself, from his midst: a ruler from among the people, not a foreign king
decisions.reason: The leader will be an Israelite, as the law required of a king (Deuteronomy 17:15), and no longer a foreign master (verse 8). The form translated "from him" can also be read "from us"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: I will bring him near, and he will approach me: the ruler given a place close to God, as a priest has
decisions.reason: "Bring near" and "approach" are words used of priests who serve in God's presence (Numbers 16:5, 9-10; Exodus 28:1). The future ruler will stand close to God by God's own invitation (compare Psalm 110:4). The verse continues the promise of the king of verse 9.

decisions.choice: pledge his heart: stake his life
decisions.reason: The verb means to give something as a pledge or guarantee (Genesis 43:9). To pledge one's heart is to put oneself at risk. Coming near God without his call meant death (Numbers 17:28; 18:7).

decisions.choice: dare to risk his life (B); No one would dare ... unless I invited him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the meaning of the idiom (m3). Readable turns the question into a plain statement and says what it implies: it is only by the LORD's invitation that anyone can come so near.

records.source: וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And you will be to me for a people, and I will be to you for God.
pieces: So you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and I will be your God.

L.22: And you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and I will be your God.

R.22: You will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q and I will be your God.

decisions.choice: you will be my people, and I will be your God: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: These words sum up the covenant from the exodus on (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Jeremiah uses them in 7:23, 11:4 and 24:7, and again in the promises of 31:1, 31:33 and 32:38.

decisions.choice: verse 22 kept, as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah does not have this verse. The Hebrew text, which this translation follows, has it.

decisions.choice: you will be my people, and I will be your God
decisions.reason: The covenant promise is worded as in 24:7 and 11:4, here with "you" because the people are spoken to directly.

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה׀סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה סַ֖עַר מִתְגּוֹרֵ֑ר עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל׃
records.gloss: Look, [the] storm of Yahweh, wrath has gone out, a sweeping tempest; on [the] head of [the] wicked it will whirl.
pieces: Look, the storm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Fury has burst out, \q a whirlwind sweeping on; \q it will crash down on the heads of the wicked.

L.23: Look, the storm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Wrath has gone out, \q a sweeping tempest; \q on the head of the wicked it will whirl down.

R.23: Look! The anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is like a storm. \q It has broken out like a whirlwind, \q and it will strike the heads of wicked people.

decisions.choice: verses 23-24 repeat 23:19-20 with small differences
decisions.reason: The two verses come back almost word for word from 23:19-20. The differences: the verb describing the tempest is not the one in 23:19 (there "whirling"; here a word for sweeping or raging), the tempest is not joined to the storm with "and", verse 24 says "the fierce anger" where 23:20 says "the anger", and verse 24 lacks the closing "with understanding" of 23:20. In chapter 23 the storm answers the false prophets; here it falls on the oppressors of verses 16 and 20.

decisions.choice: the storm of the LORD: his anger pictured as a violent storm
decisions.reason: As in 23:19, wind and storm picture God's judgment coming suddenly and with force (4:11-13; 25:32).

decisions.choice: sweeping: a tempest rushing on
decisions.reason: The form of this verb is rare. It is usually taken to describe a storm that drags or sweeps everything along; the sense is close to "whirling" in 23:19.

decisions.choice: the wording of 23:19, with "sweeping" for the different verb
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording from 23:19 so the repeat can be recognized, changing only what the Hebrew changes (m1).

records.source: לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה עַד־עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד־הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Not will turn back [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh until he has done and until he has carried out [the] purposes of his heart; in [the] latter part of the days you will understand it.
pieces: The fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not turn away \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has fully carried out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has purposed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart. \q In the days ahead you will understand this.

L.24: The fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not turn back \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done and until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has carried out the purposes of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart. \q In the latter days you will understand it.

R.24: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not stop being fiercely angry \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned. \q Later on, you will understand this.

decisions.choice: the fierce anger: a fuller phrase than 23:20
decisions.reason: 23:20 has "the anger of the LORD"; here it is "the burning of the anger", his fierce anger, as in 4:8 and 25:37. See also the note at verse 23.

decisions.choice: the latter days: the time to come, after the judgment
decisions.reason: As in 23:20, the phrase means the later part of time, the future as seen from now (48:47; 49:39). Then the people will see what the LORD intended.

decisions.choice: you will understand it: you (plural), the people, will understand the LORD's purpose
decisions.reason: "It" is the LORD's storm and the plan behind it. Unlike 23:20, the verb is not strengthened by the noun "understanding".

decisions.choice: the wording of 23:20, with "fierce" added and "clearly" left out
decisions.reason: Each level follows its wording from 23:20 closely, changing what the Hebrew changes (m1, m3); Balanced keeps the 23:20 wording but for "fierce" and the last line.
